dossier.architecture: Fixed-heading adjustable-hood scorer, gated feeder and telescopic/pivot traversal climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve provides chassis aiming rather than a turret.
subsystems.intake: Roller collector repeatedly simplified to eliminate pinch points.
subsystems.transfer: Pneumatic gate separates stored cargo from shooter; kicker controls feed speed. Two sensors stop collection at capacity.
subsystems.scoring: Lighter Colson main wheels and back wheels tune recovery and exit spin; Limelight sets aim/hood.
subsystems.endgame: Compact telescopic arms and retaining hooks support repeated rung transfers with a pneumatic angle change.
subsystems.controls: Automatic capacity logic and targeting; climb actions sequenced around hook engagement.

versions: Removed unnecessary edge wheels and support bar that trapped cargo. Added/adjusted feeder restraint and kicker.
dossier.analysis: A strong example of improving flow by removing contact geometry. More rollers and more grip can create new trapping modes rather than increase intake reliability.

context_documents.title: 2022-111 · Removing contact points can improve cargo flow
context_documents.body:
# 2022-111: Removing contact points can improve cargo flow

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The collector was repeatedly revised to remove dead zones and pinch points. A pneumatic gate separates stored cargo from the launcher, with a kicker and two capacity sensors. The retained source distinguishes main/back-wheel choices and a sequential traversal climb.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly ties collector iteration to reliable acquisition rather than simply higher roller speed.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A gate decouples possession from launch readiness. More grip can create an unwanted stable pinch, so the test must include side-by-side cargo and partial entry, not only single clean pickups.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure jam/recovery frequency and feed latency with worn cargo; test gate timing during wheel recovery.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: WildStang team interview at Central Illinois
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
source_reviews.facts: Team describes eliminating pinch points, a pneumatic feed gate, hood and chassis aiming, and repeated hook transfers.
source_reviews.limitations: Automatic captions contain terminology errors and deictic references. No dimensions derived from them.

source_reviews.title: WildStang 2022 code release and operator notes
source_reviews.locator: Post 12, driver controls and autonomous sections
source_reviews.facts: Documents heading locks, intake-facing travel mode, and autonomous approach offsets.

source_reviews.title: WildStang 2022 competition source
source_reviews.facts: Two cargo inputs and camera/translation-dependent aim code. ClimbMotion is commented out.
source_reviews.limitations: Snapshot differs in scope from team interview and does not establish match deployment.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: WildStang fit a full two-cargo path, fixed-azimuth high-hub shooter and traversal climber on a compact swerve chassis. The intake and feeder could collect from one heading while swerve translated in another direction. Before release, the chassis itself became the yaw axis. On the hangar, compact packaging depended on sequentially transferring the chassis weight between two sets of hooks.
source_review.piece_flow: Compliant pickup wheels bring cargo onto paired belt surfaces over the bumper. A polycarbonate guide leads into the upward feed. Low and high sensors indicate queue occupancy. A pneumatic gate restrains cargo before a powered kicker meters it into the shooter, where a Colson flywheel and backing wheels accelerate it through an adjustable hood.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The roughly right-angle feed packs the queue near the launcher but creates a junction where incoming cargo can be lifted prematurely. The team replaced a bare crossbar interface with a long spacer to constrain that motion. The climb keeps its envelope small in part by repeating one load transfer rather than deploying a dedicated arm for every rung.

subsystems.name: Collector
subsystems.construction: Compliant wheels and paired belt surfaces feeding over the bumper.
subsystems.operation: Capture from the floor and guide cargo through the bumper crossing.
subsystems.team_rationale: Remove dead zones and pinch points uncovered in prototyping.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Removing contact elements can eliminate a wedge rather than simply reduce grip. Test the outer approach with the chassis translating sideways.
subsystems.interfaces: Roller speeds, belt tracking, bumper height and guide edge.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check dropped or scuffed balls and debris at the approach to the guide.
subsystems.unknowns: Installed wheel diameters and belt transmission.

subsystems.name: Queue and kicker
subsystems.construction: Polycarbonate guide, two occupancy sensors, pneumatic gate and independently powered kicker.
subsystems.operation: Team describes stopping feed when full and releasing cargo to the kicker on demand.
subsystems.team_rationale: Avoid driving through the gate and reduce variation entering the flywheel.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Separate queue pressure from shot feed velocity. Validate the loaded gate under a stalled sensor and the second ball against first-shot recovery.
subsystems.interfaces: Intake belt, gate timing, kicker and flywheel.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check false occupancy, gate bounce and reverse-clear access.

subsystems.name: Fixed-azimuth shooter and drive
subsystems.construction: Swerve, Limelight, adjustable hood, Colson flywheel and backing wheels.
subsystems.operation: Vision informs hood and chassis alignment. Release code includes camera-angle ranging and translation-dependent adjustments.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team chose chassis aiming because it already had swerve, and lighter flywheels for faster recharge.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Check time from collecting to shooting while defended. Lower wheel inertia can shorten spin-up while increasing speed droop unless recovery and feed spacing are coordinated.
subsystems.interfaces: Heading controller, target detection, hood, kicker and flywheel.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check target dropout, false range, and driver override when automatic yaw conflicts with escape.
subsystems.unknowns: Measured dispersion and whether motion corrections were deployed at the filmed regional.

subsystems.name: Traversal hooks
subsystems.construction: Extending hooks plus a second set of retaining hooks.
subsystems.operation: Reach and retract onto a rung, transfer the load to retaining hooks, then extend toward the next rung and repeat.
subsystems.team_rationale: Preserve a small chassis footprint for navigating traffic.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A transfer has to be verified with the robot hanging and swinging, since static bar clearance alone misses the approach angle.
subsystems.interfaces: Hangar rungs, chassis approach and hook reset.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test partial engagement, missed reset and asymmetric catch.
subsystems.unknowns: Hook actuation and confirmed match logic.

revisions: Team removed two compliant wheels and a rear support bar after observing jams and added a spacer to constrain the upward transition.
transferable_principles: Treat each guide, roller and crossmember as part of the piece envelope. Separate retention from launch feed so each can be tuned independently.
disconfirming_conditions: A compact 90-degree path can fail if a different ball rebounds or bridges. Chassis aiming loses value when scoring heading prevents evasive translation.
remaining_gaps: Older dossier used for navigation. Public Ballpath.java has low and high inputs but does not corroborate the filmed two-full stop in the inspected update routine. The published climb files are commented out.
recommended_images: Select a dated side frame at 2:32–4:29 showing the bumper-to-kicker path and a loaded climb frame showing which hooks support the robot.
